Nestor. King of Pylos and the eldest statesman of the Greek forces at Troy, he earned the respect of his peers through his wisdom and experience rather than through superhuman martial prowess. Among all the Greek warriors, Nestor was the oldest and had survived the conflicts of previous generations, making him a living link to the heroic past. His voice in the Greek councils carried great weight, and he served as both counselor and peacemaker throughout the ten-year war. Repeatedly he mediated between Agamemnon and Achilles during their bitter quarrels, often the only voice capable of tempering their rage. Nestor was known for his lengthy speeches, filled with historical references and wisdom drawn from his long life. Yet despite his age, he was not merely an advisor but a warrior himself. He fought bravely in many encounters, standing firm against the great Hector multiple times and refusing to yield even when younger men might have faltered. When the war finally ended, Nestor was one of the fortunate few who escaped Troy alive and successfully returned home. In Homer's Odyssey he appears as a revered elder, one of the few heroes who survived the war to tell its stories to a new generation.
